title: What does the XRPL DisableMaster account flag mean?
abstract: Sourced explanation of DisableMaster and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, DisableMaster prevents the account's master key from authorizing transactions. [1]

The ledger requires another signing method, such as a regular key or signer list, before enabling the option. Disabling master signing does not erase the account, rotate its address or disable every other key. Confirm the alternative method works and retain a recovery plan before signing the change; an unusable quorum can strand control. [1][2]

XRPL distinguishes an AccountSet option from the AccountRoot bit that records the resulting state. SetFlag and ClearFlag use option identifiers, while the ledger Flags field stores bit values; the numbers are not interchangeable. Read the documented mapping for DisableMaster and check the validated account state after any permitted change. A successful submission response alone does not establish that the requested state is final. [1][2]

Author interpretation: document why DisableMaster is needed, who may authorize a change and what existing users would experience. Review irreversible settings before issuance and test reversible settings with representative counterparties. This is guidance for interpreting account controls, not a live network measurement. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
